title: Intro: Apollo GPU Systems + Redwood Partnership
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Apollo GPU Systems to explore reseller and co-sell opportunities, technical integration points for private and dedicated deployments, and potential pilot for joint customers focused on low-latency inference. Apollo interested in marketplace listing and capacity-exchange model. Redwood to share partnership deck, Apollo to share HW spec sheet and pricing bands.
topics: Integration options: marketplace listing, referral, dedicated racks
next_steps: Redwood to send partner one-pager + partnership deck (Sofia)
Apollo to share hardware spec sheet & rack pricing (Maya)
Schedule technical deep-dive with infra team (Liam + Wei) - target next week
Agree pilot success criteria and sample workload for benchmark
action_items: Owner: Sofia Martinez; Item: Share Redwood partner deck + integration checklist; Due: 2026-11-12
Owner: Maya Patel; Item: Send Apollo HW spec sheet and indicative pricing bands; Due: 2026-11-13
Owner: Liam Chen; Item: Prepare list of model/quantization compatibility questions for Apollo infra; Due: 2026-11-11
Owner: Dr. Wei Zhou; Item: Provide details on GPU SKUs, NVLink topology, and expected latency for 2k context; Due: 2026-11-14
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sofia from Redwood, AE on the partnerships team, we have Liam Chen from SE and Priya on the call too.
[00:07] Maya Patel: Hi hi, Maya here, thanks for setting this up. Really excited to talk through how Apollo and Redwood might work together.
[00:12] Darren Kline: Hey all, Darren joining from sales, quick note on timing we have a couple customers asking about turnkey private clusters.
[00:18] Sofia Martinez: Great, that's helpful context. Maybe start with you Maya—can you give a quick overview of Apollo's product and what you're looking for in partners.
[00:27] Maya Patel: Sure—Apollo builds GPU racks optimized for inference workloads, we do a mix of on-prem and colo, and cloud-hosted offering. Our newer "A10x" SKUs are targeted at low-latency chat and multi-turn workloads, we also bundle networking and a managed orchestration layer we call Apollo-Bridge, spelled B-R-I-D-G-E.
[00:40] Dr. Wei Zhou: Jumping in, our key differentiator is NVLink mesh and a faster PCIe fabric for KV cache locality, we see better tail latency for long-context models, especially when combined with our compiler optimizations.
[00:52] Liam Chen: Interesting—how does Apollo-Bridge present APIs for orchestration? Is there an operator or a managed control plane?
[01:00] Hannah Lee: It's both—customers can opt into our managed control plane or run a customer-managed operator in their VPC. We expose a REST API and have terraform modules.
[01:09] Priya Desai: Got it. From Redwood's side we care about a few integration points: 1) deploying Redwood Private into a customer VPC or onto dedicated Apollo racks, 2) network/topology constraints for KV cache and batching, 3) provisioning and billing integration if we resell or list on your marketplace.
[01:26] Maya Patel: Makes sense. On marketplace, we do revenue share or referral models; some partners want reserved capacity where we carve out pools.
[01:33] Darren Kline: Can you talk about typical commit sizes? Our sales team wants to understand what a minimum contract looks like.
[01:38] Maya Patel: For dedicated racks we usually look at 3–6 month minimums; pricing depends on rack density and support SLAs. We'll share bands after the call.
[01:45] Sofia Martinez: Cool. Liam, do you want to dig into technical compatibility—models, quantization, runtimes?
[01:51] Liam Chen: Yeah—first question: which frameworks and runtimes does Apollo-Bridge support? We rely on Triton and custom kernels for some quantized paths.
[01:58] Hannah Lee: We currently support Triton, a custom runtime we call "ApolloRT" and standard container workflows. For quantized models we support int8 and 4-bit Q/KV optimizations, though some customers use third-party libs.
[02:10] Liam Chen: Good, on the Redwood runtime we do kernel selection for attention patterns and we have a quantization-friendly path. Any constraints around exposing NVLink or PCIe to guest VMs?
[02:19] Dr. Wei Zhou: For dedicated racks it's baremetal or host-tenant with passthrough; NVLink is available in baremetal and in our managed kube we can expose RDMA. There may be some tenant isolation overhead.
[02:30] Priya Desai: Noted—latency SLOs matter for our customers. Do you have typical 95th/99th tail numbers for single-turn responses at 2k tokens?
[02:40] Dr. Wei Zhou: Ballpark 95th is 120–140ms for 2k context on our A10x optimized stack; 99th jumps a bit depending on multi-tenant noise, but we can run controlled benchmarks.
[02:51] Sofia Martinez: That's helpful—sounds promising. From a security standpoint, our enterprise customers will ask about SOC2, SAML/SSO, and KMS for key management. Do you have those controls?
[03:00] Hannah Lee: We are SOC2 in progress, we support SAML SSO, and we integrate with customer KMS or HSMs for key storage. Audit logs are available in our managed control plane.
[03:10] Darren Kline: On the commercial side, what's your appetite to be listed on Redwood's partner marketplace vs a revenue share referral model?
[03:17] Sofia Martinez: We typically support both—marketplace listing helps drive customers into an easy procurement flow; reserved capacity and co-sell are good for larger accounts. We can align on margins later.
[03:26] Maya Patel: We're open to both; initial focus is to prove the integration with a pilot and then go marketing-led.
[03:31] Liam Chen: For the pilot, we'd want a sample workload, models to test (e.g., Llama2-70B quantized, and a 7B chat model), and clear success metrics—latency, token cost, and availability.
[03:41] Priya Desai: We'll also want to test prefix and KV caching behavior since Redwood optimizes for caching to lower cost—does Apollo-Bridge allow sticky routing or can we colocate caching nodes?
[03:50] Dr. Wei Zhou: We do support sticky placement and can reserve nodes for caching; we'll need to coordinate on network topology.
[03:57] Hannah Lee: I'll add that we can provide access to a staging rack for benchmarking.
[04:02] Maya Patel: Also FYI, some of our customers require data residency and audit trails; we often run private deployments in region-specific colos.
[04:11] Sofia Martinez: That's fine—Redwood supports private VPC deployments and on-prem packages; we can map compliance controls to your managed offering.
[04:19] Darren Kline: Any blockers you see from the Apollo side for a pilot?
[04:23] Dr. Wei Zhou: Nothing major; we need integration details—API contracts, expected throughput, and any special kernel requirements.
[04:30] Liam Chen: We'll draft a short tech spec and share it. Also, can you share the scheduler or orchestration docs for Apollo-Bridge?
[04:36] Hannah Lee: Yes, sending after the call.
[04:39] Sofia Martinez: Great. A couple of miscellaneous items: are there exclusivity expectations? Some partners ask for territory carve-outs.
[04:46] Maya Patel: Not at this stage. We'd prefer open partnerships but may discuss preferred partners for specific enterprise accounts.
[04:52] Priya Desai: Good to know. On metrics, we'll want to instrument latency and cost per token in the Redwood console and correlate billing to your meter. Can Apollo surface per-token usage and per-route logs?
[05:03] Hannah Lee: We can emit metrics and logs to external monitoring and provide usage reports.
[05:08] Sofia Martinez: Excellent. Ok, let's recap and confirm next steps—Sofia to share Redwood partner deck, Apollo to share HW specs and pricing bands, Liam and Wei to schedule a technical deep-dive, and both teams to agree on pilot workload. We'll aim to reconvene next Tuesday for the deep-dive.
[05:25] Maya Patel: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[05:28] Darren Kline: Thanks, talk soon.
[05:30] Sofia Martinez: Thanks all — I'll follow up with calendar invites and the deck.

[Notes]
- Shared links: Redwood partner one-pager: https://redwood.ai/partners/deck-apollo.pdf; Apollo staging rack spec: https://apollo-gpu.com/specs/a10x-staging.pdf
- Mentioned models for pilot: Llama2-70B-quantized, Redwood-chat-7B (customer name paraphrased in call)
- Transcript has occasional mis-hearings (e.g., Apollo-Bridge sometimes transcribed as Apollo Bridge/Apolo-Bridge).
